name: Anvil
description: A heavy block of steel that the hot metal is hammered on. Its flat face, horn and holes each have a different job.

name: Hammer
description: The smith's main tool. A cross-peen hammer, with one flat face and one wedge-shaped face, is the most common.

name: Tongs
description: Used to hold metal that is far too hot to touch. Smiths often forge their own tongs to fit each project.

name: Forge
description: The fire itself, fed with coal, charcoal or gas, and blown with air to reach forging temperatures.

name: Stakes
description: Small anvils that sit in the hardy hole of the anvil, for shaping curves and hollows.

name: Drawing out
description: Strike after strike, a thick bar grows long and thin. Patience, turned into shape.

name: Upsetting
description: The reverse of drawing out. Hammer the hot end and the bar gets shorter and thicker.

name: Bending
description: Over the horn of the anvil, straight steel turns into hooks, rings and scrolls.

name: Forge welding
description: Two pieces, almost white hot, hammered fast until they become one.

name: Quenching
description: Glowing steel meets cold oil. A hiss, a cloud of steam, and the blade is hard.

name: Tempering
description: A gentle reheat after the quench. The steel turns straw, then bronze, then purple, and stops being brittle.
